# Windows SQLite filenames

The isolated executable check of chat/import commit `9745b9a` passed bundle integrity and production dependency imports, then stopped before daemon readiness. A new bounded daemon diagnostic reported `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR` / SQLite error 14 at `StudioStore`'s 306-character database filename. The generic launcher error mentioned a possible port conflict; no port conflict was established.

A separate probe used the candidate's actual Node v24.21.0 against new owned files. A plain 364-character database filename failed to open. A 369-character canonical filename, passed with Windows' four-character extended-path prefix, opened, enabled WAL and FULL synchronization, committed a transaction, read it back and closed. The failed executable profile and original checkout were preserved. No provider inference or Studio operation occurred.

`sqliteTransportPath` converts the filename only at the native `DatabaseSync` boundary in StudioStore, WorkStore, ConversationWorkStore, WorkflowStore, LearningStore and the Codex action journal. Existing canonical paths continue to drive validation, project identity, locks, sidecar checks and display. The adapter supplies no filesystem authority or validation. It preserves empty temporary filenames, exact `:memory:`, existing namespace/device spellings and non-Windows behavior. Database options, schemas, state layout and operation deadlines remain unchanged.

The build passed with 266 explicit sources. All four new regressions passed on the candidate's actual Node v24.21.0 without skips: temporary/in-memory filename compatibility, deep WAL transactions with rollback and durable reopen, real store identity persistence, and actual daemon initialization and clean parent-loss shutdown across all six deep databases. Authenticated metadata reads explicitly open the lazy learning and workflow stores. Each database is a direct single-link file with WAL mode and a passing SQLite quick check after shutdown; canonical project metadata remains unchanged.

The daemon fixture keeps its working directory at 220 characters while the unchanged SHA-scoped layout puts every database beyond 306 characters. Its home is a fresh short child of the real canonical home, with separate AppData/temp paths and cleanup limited to the exact owned directories after confirmed successful shutdown. A read-only native trace confirmed that an earlier fake home beneath TEMP correctly failed the existing dangerous-ancestor permission guard. The product permission policy was unchanged; existing account, receipt and failed executable state were preserved.

The ten affected storage, HTTP and private-permission suites passed 130/130 cases without skips (91.184 seconds), including native owner/private-key refusal and unchanged permission-equivalence cases. Together with the four new regressions, this checkpoint passed 134/134 cases. Local logs are `runtime/sqlite-path-build.log`, `runtime/sqlite-path-focused.log` and `runtime/sqlite-path-regression.log`.

The green chat/import PR remains a separate milestone. A fresh isolated packaged-executable check is still required. Until it succeeds, the earlier executable launch remains failed and customer acceptance is unverified. The executable candidate is unsigned; SSH commit verification is separate from application signing. No provider inference or Studio operation was performed.
